If you are looking for a web design company in Atlanta and you are one person with a trade, a client list and a phone, you have probably noticed that most agencies are not really talking to you. Their case studies feature firms with staff and budgets. Their prices are behind a discovery call. Dominion Web Design Pro is built the other way around: prices printed, a free demo before you pay, every page written by hand, and the site yours to keep.

We are a small web design business based in Big Sandy, East Texas, and we build for Atlanta businesses remotely. We will not pretend to have an Atlanta address. What we can offer is a straight price and a real site you can see first.

Atlanta's small business economy runs on owners, not departments

LendingTree has ranked metro Atlanta first among the largest U.S. metros for its share of Black-owned businesses four years running. In its latest study, which uses 2023 Census data, 10.7% of the metro's businesses with employees are Black-owned, against 3.4% nationally. Fayetteville, North Carolina and Washington, D.C. came next.

Those are businesses with payroll. Behind them sit many more one-person operations: barbers in the West End, caterers who work out of a shared kitchen, mobile detailers, braiders, tax preparers, personal trainers in Midtown. The Atlanta Wealth Building Initiative has reported a wide gap in what these businesses are worth, about $58,085 on average for a Black-owned business in Atlanta against $658,264 for a white-owned one. A business at that scale cannot carry a five-figure website and a monthly retainer, so the agencies never call, and the owner decides a real website is not for them. That is a pricing problem, not a quality problem.

Where a website matters most in Atlanta

Food is one of the most visible small business categories in the city: restaurants, catering, bakeries and food trucks from Old Fourth Ward to the Westside. These businesses live or die on being found at the moment someone is hungry and searching. Plenty of them run on an Instagram account and a phone number in a bio link. That works until a customer types "catering near me" into Google and finds someone else.

Health and personal care is just as big. LendingTree's study found that 26.2% of Black-owned businesses nationwide were in health care and social assistance in 2023: home care agencies, therapists, child care providers, medical billing. Those owners sell trust, and a prospective client checks the website before calling. A clear page that lists services, credentials you actually hold and how to book is the minimum.

Service trades come next. A plumber in Southwest Atlanta, a cleaning company covering Buckhead and Sandy Springs, a mobile mechanic working the I-285 loop: their customers search by job and neighborhood. A site with one page per service, the areas covered and a tap-to-call number at the top answers those searches in a way a social profile cannot.

What every Atlanta site we build includes

  • A contact form that is tested so messages actually reach your inbox.
  • Real words about your business, written from a conversation with you.
  • Ownership: the domain and the content are yours, not leased back to you.

Dominion Web Design Pro works out of East Texas. A website is not poured concrete. Nobody needs to stand in your parking lot to build one. What has to happen is a conversation about what your business does, who calls you and what you want the site to make happen, and that conversation works the same on the phone from Buckhead as it does across a desk.

What we will not do is pretend to know your market better than you do. A barber in the West End knows his block. A caterer in Decatur knows which venues send her work. The job is to turn that knowledge into a site that gets found, not to explain Atlanta to an Atlantan. Free help for Atlanta small businesses

  • Invest AtlantaThe city's development authority runs Small Business Resource Centers through its ATLinBusiness program, with no-cost one-on-one consulting in person or online.
  • Georgia SBDC at Georgia StateThe metro Atlanta office of the University of Georgia's Small Business Development Center network, housed at Georgia State's Robinson College of Business, helps with business plans and marketing.
  • SCORE AtlantaVolunteer mentors and workshops, a resource partner of the U.S. Small Business Administration.

Those groups can help with your plan and your financing. When you are ready for the website, ask the same four questions of everyone you talk to: what does it cost in dollars, do I own the site and domain, what does a change cost in six months, and can I see one you built for a business my size. Ask us too.

Common questions

How much does a web design company in Atlanta charge a small business?

Many Atlanta agencies do not publish prices, and custom builds can run into the thousands before any monthly fees. Dominion Web Design Pro prints its prices: $497 for a 5-page Starter site, $997 for Pro and $1,997 for Agency, one time. Hosting, maintenance and updates are $49 a month, or included while you keep the AI agent.

Can a company outside Atlanta build a good website for an Atlanta business?

Yes, for most small businesses. Website work is done by phone, email and shared links whether the designer is in Midtown or in Texas. What you give up is in-person meetings. If you want someone at your office every month, hire locally. If you want a clear, fast site at a printed price, location matters much less.

Do I need a website if my business runs on Instagram and Facebook?

A social page is rented space: the platform controls who sees it and can change the rules any day. A website is yours, shows up in Google searches, and gives customers one link with your hours, services, prices and booking. Keep the social accounts and link them from the site.

What should I ask an Atlanta web designer before hiring?

Ask for the price in dollars, whether you will own the site and the domain, what a change costs six months from now, and to see a site built for a business your size. A designer who avoids any of those four is telling you something.

Can I see an Atlanta website demo before I pay anything?

Yes. Request the free demo with your business name and trade and you get a link to a preview site. You decide after you have looked at it on your phone.

See your website before you pay for it

Give us your business name and what you do, and a demo site gets built for you to look at on your own phone. If you like it, pick a package. If you do not, you have spent nothing but the minute it took to look.
